Hello, and welcome back to Speak Up, the show for people who live in a second language. Today's topic is a feeling that every one of you knows: being nervous. When I moved to Canada, I used to stay quiet in work meetings. I was afraid of making a mistake. Then a colleague told me something that I have never forgotten. She said that people do not remember your mistakes. They remember your ideas. So this week, here is your challenge. Say one thing in a meeting, or in a shop, that you usually keep inside. It is going to feel strange. Do it anyway.

Hi, Ana Paula! It's Juliana. Guess what? I passed! I got the results this morning, and I have been smiling all day. Do you remember last year, when I almost gave up? I told you that my English wasn't good enough. You said that I just needed time, and you were right. I studied every night after work, and I practiced with my patients. Tonight, my husband and I are going to celebrate at that little Italian restaurant on St. George Street. You have to come! And next year, it's your turn. I know you're going to make it.

When I arrived in Florida, I was very nervous. At first, I used to answer everything with yes or no. Then my neighbor told me that my English was good. Since then, I have taken a small risk every week. Next month, I am going to celebrate my first year here.
